rationale: The workflow already implements Gradle dependency caching via `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v6.4.1` with `cache-read-only: true`, and uses `actions/cache/restore@v6`/`actions/cache/save@v6` for the IntelliJ Platform test cache and Gradle TestKit cache. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (supported by experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200 showing 20.4% elapsed savings) has a contraindication "An equivalent cache already exists" that applies here because Gradle dependency caching is already configured. No other pattern fits this single-job reusable priming workflow: there is no matrix for fail-fast, no scheduled runs for cancel-stale/idle-schedule, no repeated failing jobs for failed-job-first, and path filtering or workflow skipping would alter the reusable workflow's intended contract. Adding another cache step for the same dependency directory would be redundant and could conflict with the existing setup-gradle cache management.
